title: Responder rotation synthesis and deferred postmortem protocol
author: Priya Shah
content:
Overview:

This playbook describes Redwood's responder rotation synthesis process and a lightweight Deferred Postmortem (DPM) protocol for incidents that meet defined criteria. It combines on-call scheduling practices, a structured bridge handoff procedure, and customer-facing messaging templates designed for speed and clarity. The goal is to reduce cognitive load during high-impact events and to ensure timely learning when full postmortems are not immediately practical.

Scope:
- Applies to: SRE, Serving Runtime, Platform, and Incident Response stakeholders.
- Excludes: low-priority alerts that resolve without human intervention (see 'Auto-resolved alerts' below).

Definitions:
- Responder rotation synthesis: periodic review and rebalancing of on-call shifts, handoffs, and escalation ladders to maintain equitable load and coverage.
- Deferred Postmortem (DPM): a time-boxed post-incident review that defers non-critical analysis until stakeholders are available, while still capturing root evidence and action items immediately.

Key principles:
1) Fast stabilization first: prioritize containment and customer impact minimization.
2) Minimal friction handoffs: standardized bridge transfer reduces repeated context overhead.
3) Continuous learning: short DPMs for low-severity incidents; full postmortems for Sev1/Sev2.
4) Equity in rotations: no responder assigned >36 hours continuous duty without relief.

On-call rotation design (synthesis process):
1. Quarterly synthesis review (owner: SRE lead):
   - Pull the last quarter's on-call logs and pager counts.
   - Calculate median and 95th percentile pager counts per responder.
   - Identify top-10% busiest windows and common root causes.
2. Rebalance rules:
   - Move noisy services to a dedicated micro-rotation if they account for >25% of pages.
   - Limit night-weekend primary duty to volunteers in the rotation unless emergency staffing required.
3. Local fairness check (monthly):
   - Team leads run a 15-minute review in the first week of each month to confirm schedule fairness and swap if needed.

Rotation constraints (config):
| Constraint | Value | Rationale |
|---|---:|---|
| Max continuous on-call | 36h | Prevent fatigue and degraded decision-making |
| Minimum handoff overlap | 15m | Time to summarize bridge state and outstanding actions |
| Max weekly duty | 56h | Prevent single-responder overload across teams |
| Handoff notes retention | 90d | Auditability and incident reconstruction |

Bridge handoff procedure (step-by-step):
1) Pre-handoff checklist (outgoing):
   - Summarize incident timeline, current hypotheses, mitigation steps in progress, and customer impact.
   - Confirm runbook page(s) in Bridge tab are current and link to traces/log queries.
2) Live handoff (over bridge):
   - 5–15 minute verbal summary; ensure incoming acknowledges critical mitigations.
   - If unresolved customer-impacting work remains, assign an owner and ETA.
3) Post-handoff (incoming):
   - Record a 1-line status in the incident timeline and attach a minimum evidence set (logs, traces, alert IDs).

Incident lifecycle and DPM decision matrix:
- If incident is Sev1 or multi-tenant Sev2 -> full postmortem required within 72 hours of remediation.
- If incident meets ALL of the following, use DPM: single-tenant, <30 minutes customer-visible impact, known cause, effective mitigation applied at resolution.
- Otherwise triage for full postmortem.

Deferred Postmortem (DPM) protocol (when to use and how):
Purpose: capture essential facts and actions quickly when resource constraints or ongoing high operational tempo would make a full postmortem impractical in 72 hours.
DPM steps (owner: incident lead):
1) Within 8 hours of incident resolution: populate DPM template with
   - 1-line summary, impact window (start/end), services affected, severity, and customer impact.
   - Evidence snapshot (link to logs, runbook used, mitigation commands).
2) Create action items with clear owners and SLAs (default: 14-day action SLA).
3) Flag DPM for follow-up in the next synthesis meeting.
4) If DPM reveals systemic risk or unresolved unknowns, escalate to full postmortem.

DPM template (minimum fields):
- Title (1 line)
- Date/time window
- Affected services and teams (comma-separated)
- Immediate mitigations executed
- Evidence links (logs, traces, alert IDs)
- Action items (owner | due date | description)
- Decision to close DPM or escalate (yes/no)

Escalation and timeline expectations:
- Immediate: severity declaration and customer status update within 30 minutes of detection for Sev1/Sev2.
- Short window: initial triage and bridge stand-up within 60 minutes.
- DPM creation: within 8 hours.
- Full postmortem: published within 72 hours for Sev1/Sev2.

Customer communications templates (for bridge operator use):
- Initial status (first 30m):
  "We have identified an issue affecting [feature/service]. Our team has engaged and is investigating. We will provide an update within 30 minutes."

- Follow-up status (post-triage):
  "Update: The issue is caused by [brief cause]. Mitigations underway include [actions]. Current impact: [scope]. Next update scheduled at [time/ETA]."

- Resolution notice:
  "Resolved: The issue affecting [service] has been mitigated at [time]. Root cause and next steps will be published in a follow-up note or postmortem."

- SLA-credit preliminary message (if applicable):
  "We are assessing impact against our SLA commitments. If you are eligible, we will follow up with credit details once our postmortem is complete."

Game day design and schedule (90-minute template):
- Goal: validate handoff, DPM creation, and customer comms speed.
- Attendees: 1 bridge operator, 2 responders, 1 product EM, 1 customer success observer.
- Timeline:
  00:00 — Inject alert and distribute pager
  00:05 — Bridge up and first customer status sent
  00:20 — Handoff simulation between responders
  00:45 — DPM skeleton completed and action items assigned
  01:05 — Demo of status page update flow and mock SLA notice
  01:20 — 15-minute retro and lessons logged

Runbook snippets (examples):
- Quick KV-cache eviction (serving-runtime):
  "# Commands
  kubectl exec -n runtime svc/cache-operator -- cache evict --pattern=*
  # Verify: tail logs for 200 responses to health endpoint for 5m"

- Throttle mitigation (traffic spike):
  "1) Move non-critical traffic to burst_throttle=true route.
   2) Increase instance headroom by policy 'scale-now' for model-serving service.
   3) Notify customers via status page if >5% error rate persists after 5m."

Ownership and metrics (who owns what):
- On-call synthesis owner: SRE manager (quarterly cadence).
- DPM governance: Incident review council (product + SRE rep)
- Bridge operator: maintains status templates and runbook links.
- Metrics to track: mean time to ack (MTTA), mean time to remediate (MTTR), percentage of incidents resolved with DPM, action-item closure rate within 14 days.

Audit and retention:
- DPMs and postmortems retained for 2 years in the incident archive.
- Handoff notes retained for 90 days.

Related pages and references:
- Link: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-evidence-collection-standard (internal)
- Link: /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/kv-cache-eviction (internal)

Appendix: triage decision quick chart:
- High latency + multi-tenant -> Sev1 -> full postmortem
- Short outage <30m + single-tenant + known fix -> DPM
- Repeated flapping events -> escalate to hypothesis-driven postmortem
